paragraphes: At school, there are rules. Someone writes them. Someone checks that we follow them. Someone decides when to change them.
The school supervisor is not the only person who cares. The head teacher and the other leaders care too.
A company protects its data in the same way. This is called security governance.

decouverte.titre: It is like the school rules
decouverte.comme: The school rules say what you can do. The leaders check that people follow them. Everyone has a role.
decouverte.enVrai: A policy is a rule that the company writes. A procedure is a list of steps for a task. Security governance is the set of roles, policies, and procedures that guide how a company protects its data. The picture stops here: school rules are not about data.

decouverte.question: A company has its customer files stolen. Whose problem is it?
options: Only the IT team (IT means information technology)
The whole company, leaders included
Only the customers who lost data
decouverte.explanation: Many people think security is only for computer experts. In fact, it is a business problem.

decouverte.texte: An online toy shop buys a very good firewall. A firewall is a tool that blocks bad traffic. But nobody decides who can see the customer files. Nobody checks the rules. Tools are not enough. You also need decisions, roles, and checks.

decouverte.comme: At school, the head teacher and the school board decide the big rules. The teachers apply them.
decouverte.enVrai: In a company, executive management leads governance. The board of directors often helps. The board watches the managers for the owners of the company. Security governance often overlaps with two other kinds. Overlap means they cover some of the same ground. Corporate governance directs the whole company. IT governance directs the computer systems.

decouverte.titre: A process, like handing in homework
decouverte.comme: To hand in homework, you follow the same steps each time: write it, read it again, hand it in, get a grade.
decouverte.enVrai: A process is a series of actions that you repeat in the same way. Governance covers all the processes that define and manage the security rules. It also includes oversight. Oversight means watching and checking that people follow the rules. The manual gives a second definition of governance, and it is about processes.

cards.question: Official definition: “security governance”
cards.answer: Security governance is the set of responsibilities, policies, and procedures related to defining, managing, and overseeing security practices at an organization.
cards.explanation: In simple words: governance is who is responsible, what the rules are, and how the company checks them.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Evaluate and Apply Security Governance Principles”. You will need to know this sentence word for word.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “security governance”?
options: Security governance is the set of tools, policies, and procedures related to defining, managing, and overseeing security practices at an organization.
Security governance is the set of responsibilities, policies, and procedures related to buying, installing, and updating security tools at an organization.
Security governance is the set of responsibilities, policies, and procedures related to defining, managing, and overseeing security practices at an organization.
Security governance is the set of responsibilities, policies, and procedures related to defining, managing, and overseeing security practices in the IT department.
options_why: It says tools instead of responsibilities. Governance starts with who is responsible, not with products.
It talks only about tools. Governance is about defining, managing, and overseeing security practices.
It says the IT department only. Governance covers the whole organization.
cards.answer: Security governance is the set of responsibilities, policies, and procedures related to defining, managing, and overseeing security practices at an organization.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: responsibilities, policies, procedures, and defining, managing, overseeing.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “security governance” from memory.
cards.answer: Security governance is the set of responsibilities, policies, and procedures related to defining, managing, and overseeing security practices at an organization.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the set of responsibilities, policies, and procedures; three actions; and security practices.

cards.question: Official definition: “security governance” as a set of processes
cards.answer: Security governance is the set of all organizational processes involved in defining and managing information security policies and procedures, including the oversight to ensure that those policies and procedures follow the direction of the organization's strategy and mission.
cards.explanation: This is the second definition. It stresses the processes and the oversight that checks them.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Organizational Processes”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “security governance”?
options: Security governance is the set of all organizational processes involved in defining and managing information security policies and procedures, including the oversight to ensure that those policies and procedures follow the direction of the organization's strategy and mission.

Security governance is the set of all technical processes involved in defining and managing information security policies and procedures, including the oversight to ensure that those policies and procedures follow the direction of the organization's strategy and mission.

Security governance is the set of all organizational processes involved in defining and managing information security policies and procedures, including the audits to ensure that those policies and procedures follow the direction of the IT department.

Security governance is the set of all organizational processes involved in defining information security policies and procedures, without any oversight of whether those policies and procedures follow the direction of the organization's strategy and mission.
options_why: It says technical processes. The sentence is about organizational processes, led by the leaders.
It says the direction of the IT department. The direction comes from the strategy and mission of the organization.
It removes the oversight. Governance always includes oversight to check the direction.
cards.answer: Security governance is the set of all organizational processes involved in defining and managing information security policies and procedures, including the oversight to ensure that those policies and procedures follow the direction of the organization's strategy and mission.
cards.explanation: Key words: all organizational processes, defining and managing, and the oversight.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “security governance” from memory.
cards.answer: Security governance is the set of all organizational processes involved in defining and managing information security policies and procedures, including the oversight to ensure that those policies and procedures follow the direction of the organization's strategy and mission.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the processes, what they manage (policies and procedures), and the oversight that checks the direction.

cards.question: Many managers think that security is only an IT problem. What is the truth?
options: It is an IT issue, because only IT staff use security tools
It is a legal issue that only the lawyers can handle
It is a money issue, because only the finance team can handle the costs of security
It is a business issue that needs planning across the whole company
options_why: IT staff use the tools, but the data belongs to the whole company. Every department must take part.
Laws matter, but protecting data also needs daily choices from every department.
Cost matters, but security is more than a budget. It needs rules, roles, and checks.
cards.answer: It is a business issue that needs planning across the whole company
cards.explanation: Protecting assets and data needs planning and oversight from people in the whole company, not just the IT department.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Evaluate and Apply Security Governance Principles”.

cards.question: Which group MOST often leads security governance in a company?
options: The security analysts who run the tools every day
Executive management, often with the board of directors
The IT department on its own
Outside auditors who visit the company once a year to check its work
options_why: Analysts do the daily work. The top leaders lead governance.
Security is not only an IT issue. Leaders from the whole company must take part.
Auditors can check the work, but they do not lead it. The company's own leaders do.
cards.answer: Executive management, often with the board of directors
cards.explanation: Security governance is typically led by executive management, usually including the board of directors.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Evaluate and Apply Security Governance Principles”.

cards.question: Which two other kinds of governance does security governance often overlap with?
cards.answer: Corporate governance and IT governance.
cards.explanation: Security is a wide business issue, so it touches both the whole company and its computer systems.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Evaluate and Apply Security Governance Principles”.

cards.question: Which action is part of security governance?
options: Buying as many security tools as possible
Letting each worker write personal security rules
Leaving every security decision to the IT department
Defining security roles and responsibilities
options_why: Tools alone are not enough. You also need roles, rules, and checks.
Without shared rules, everybody protects in a different way and nobody checks.
Security is a business issue. Leaders and other departments must take part.
cards.answer: Defining security roles and responsibilities
cards.explanation: Governance sets who does what, under which rules, and with what checks.

cards.question: A shop buys a very good firewall. It has no security rules and no checks. Which description is BEST?
options: The firewall is too old to protect the shop
It has tools, but no governance to direct and check them
The shop needs more IT staff to run the firewall and read its reports every day
The shop needs a cheaper firewall
options_why: The age of the tool is not the problem. The lack of rules and checks is.
More staff can help, but nobody has set the rules or the checks yet.
Cost is not the problem. A better tool still needs rules and checks.
cards.answer: It has tools, but no governance to direct and check them
cards.explanation: Tools are not enough. You also need decisions, roles, policies, and checks.

cards.question: A new CEO asks who is responsible for security. Nobody can answer. What should leaders do FIRST?
options: Define the security roles and responsibilities
Buy more security tools
Ask an outside team to attack the systems
Leave the IT team to handle it alone, since it is a technical matter
options_why: Tools do not fix a lack of roles. Someone must own the decisions first.
A test can find weaknesses, but it does not say who is responsible.
Security is a business issue. The IT team cannot carry all of it alone.
cards.answer: Define the security roles and responsibilities
cards.explanation: Governance starts with clear responsibilities. Then you can write rules and check them.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Evaluate and Apply Security Governance Principles”.

cards.question: In your own words: why is security not only an IT issue?
cards.answer: Protecting data needs planning and checks from people in the whole company, not only the IT team.
cards.explanation: Every department uses company data, so every department helps to protect it.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Evaluate and Apply Security Governance Principles”.

cards.question: Which statement is NOT a reason why security is a business issue?
options: Data loss can hurt the whole company
Every department uses company data
Only IT staff use the company's data
Protection needs planning and oversight by leaders
options_why: This is a real reason. A loss can hurt customers, money, and trust.
This is a real reason. Every department must protect the data it uses.
This is a real reason. Leaders must plan and watch over security.
cards.answer: Only IT staff use the company's data
cards.explanation: Many departments use data, so many departments must help to protect it.

cards.question: Leaders check that the security rules follow the direction of the company. What is this called?
options: A procedure
Oversight
A policy
A process
options_why: A procedure is a list of steps for a task. It is not the checking.
A policy is a rule that the company writes. It is not the checking.
A process is a series of repeated actions. Oversight is the checking part of governance.
cards.answer: Oversight
cards.explanation: Oversight means watching and checking. It is a part of security governance.

cards.question: What is the difference between a policy and a procedure?
options: A policy is a list of steps for a task. A procedure is a rule that the company writes
A policy is for leaders. A procedure is for customers
They mean the same thing in a company
A policy is a rule. A procedure is a list of steps for a task
options_why: The two words are swapped. A policy is the rule, and a procedure gives the steps.
Both are for people inside the company. Neither one is for customers.
They are different. One is a rule, and the other explains how to do a task.
cards.answer: A policy is a rule. A procedure is a list of steps for a task
cards.explanation: The policy says what the rule is. The procedure says how to do the task.

cards.question: What is a process? Say it in simple words.
cards.answer: A series of actions that you repeat in the same way.
cards.explanation: Think of the steps you follow each time you hand in homework.

cards.question: Which reason BEST explains why security governance overlaps with corporate governance and IT governance?
options: Security is a wide business issue that touches the whole company
Security leaders also run the finances of the company
IT staff write every corporate rule, so they must lead all three kinds of governance
The law says the three must be one team
options_why: Security leaders do not run finances. The overlap comes from how wide security is.
IT staff do not write every rule. Security simply touches many parts of the company.
No law says this. The overlap comes from the wide reach of security.
cards.answer: Security is a wide business issue that touches the whole company
cards.explanation: Because security is a wide-ranging business issue, it commonly overlaps with both.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Evaluate and Apply Security Governance Principles”.

cards.question: What does corporate governance direct?
options: Only the computer systems
Only the security team
The whole company
Only the sales team
options_why: That is IT governance. Corporate governance covers the whole company.
Security governance is smaller. Corporate governance directs everything in the company.
Sales is one part of the company. Corporate governance directs all of it.
cards.answer: The whole company
cards.explanation: Corporate governance directs the whole company. IT governance directs its computer systems.

cards.question: What is oversight, in simple words?
cards.answer: Watching and checking that people follow the rules and the direction of the company.
cards.explanation: It is the checking part of security governance.

decouverte.titre: The entry check at the club
paragraphes: Your basketball club exists to let local kids play. One day, a new rule adds a very long check at the door of every practice.
Now nobody comes to practice. The rule protects the club, but it stops the club from doing its job.
Companies can have the same problem with security. To avoid it, they start from their mission and their business strategy.

decouverte.titre: It is like a car trip
decouverte.comme: On a trip, the mission is the place you want to reach, and why. The strategy is the route: the roads you take.
decouverte.enVrai: The mission says what the company is, what it does, and why it exists. The strategy says how the company will do it. The picture stops here: the place rarely changes, but the route can change with traffic.

decouverte.question: A security rule stops the sales team from doing its work. What does this show?
options: Security always slows a company down
The rule does not fit what the company wants to do
The sales team does not want to try
decouverte.answer: The rule does not fit what the company wants to do
decouverte.explanation: It is easy to think that security is a brake by nature. In fact, a rule that does not fit the work of the company is the problem.

decouverte.texte: Mission: sell cheap sneakers to young people. Strategy: sell mostly on phones, with a sale every month. Good security protects the payments without making buying harder. It helps the shop sell. The shop also sets goals and objectives. You will meet them in the next planet.

decouverte.comme: A car has brakes. If they are badly set, the car cannot move. If they are well set, you can drive fast and stay safe.
decouverte.enVrai: Security that does not fit the company is a business blocker. It is an obstacle that people must get past to do their work. Security that fits the company is a business enabler. It helps the company reach its goals.

cards.question: Official definition: “mission statement”
cards.answer: A mission statement is a simple declaration that defines a company's function and purpose; a mission statement summarizes what the company is, what it does, and why the company exists to do those things.
cards.explanation: In simple words: the mission says what the company is, what it does, and why it exists.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “mission statement”?
options: A mission statement is a simple declaration that defines a company's function and purpose; a mission statement summarizes what the company is, what it does, and why the company exists to do those things.
A mission statement is a detailed plan that defines a company's function and purpose; a mission statement summarizes what the company is, what it does, and why the company exists to do those things.
A mission statement is a simple declaration that defines a company's function and purpose; a mission statement summarizes what the company is, what it does, and how the company will do those things.

A mission statement is a simple declaration that defines a company's function and profit; a mission statement summarizes what the company is, what it earns, and why the company exists to do those things.
options_why: A mission statement is a simple declaration, not a detailed plan. The plan is closer to the strategy.
It says how. The mission says why the company exists. The strategy says how.
It talks about profit and earnings. The mission is about function and purpose.
cards.answer: A mission statement is a simple declaration that defines a company's function and purpose; a mission statement summarizes what the company is, what it does, and why the company exists to do those things.
cards.explanation: Key words: simple declaration, function and purpose, what it is, what it does, and why it exists.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “mission statement” from memory.
cards.answer: A mission statement is a simple declaration that defines a company's function and purpose; a mission statement summarizes what the company is, what it does, and why the company exists to do those things.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: what the company is, what it does, and why it exists.

cards.question: Official definition: “business strategy”
cards.answer: A business strategy describes the actions that a company takes to achieve its goals and objectives.
cards.explanation: In simple words: the strategy is the route. It lists the actions that the company takes to reach its goals.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”. Goals and objectives are in the next planet.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “business strategy”?
options: A business strategy describes the reasons that a company exists to achieve its goals and objectives.
A business strategy describes the actions that a company takes to avoid risk in its goals and objectives.
A business strategy describes the actions that a company takes to achieve its goals and objectives.
A business strategy describes the goals that a company expects to achieve with its actions and objectives.
options_why: Reasons to exist belong to the mission. The strategy describes actions.
The strategy is not about avoiding risk. It is about the actions that help to achieve the goals.
The words are mixed up. The strategy describes the actions that help to achieve the goals.
cards.answer: A business strategy describes the actions that a company takes to achieve its goals and objectives.
cards.explanation: Key words: describes the actions, and achieve its goals and objectives.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “business strategy” from memory.
cards.answer: A business strategy describes the actions that a company takes to achieve its goals and objectives.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the strategy, the actions that a company takes, and its goals and objectives.

cards.question: Official definition: “business enabler” (security that helps the mission)
cards.answer: In other words, a company should achieve its mission thanks in part to security, not despite security.
cards.explanation: Good security is like an engine. The company reaches its mission with the help of security.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about “business enabler” from memory.
cards.answer: In other words, a company should achieve its mission thanks in part to security, not despite security.
cards.explanation: Remember two parts: thanks in part to security, and not despite security.

cards.question: Workers say that security is an obstacle they must get past to do their work. What role does security play?
options: A business enabler
A business goal
A business objective
A business blocker
options_why: An enabler helps the company succeed. Here, security does the opposite.
A goal is a result that the company wants. It is not a role of security.
An objective is a short step toward a goal. It does not describe this problem.
cards.answer: A business blocker
cards.explanation: Security that does not fit the company becomes a business blocker.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”.

cards.question: What does the mission of a company say?
options: How the company will earn more money next year
What the company is, what it does, and why it exists
Which security tools the security team will buy during the next year
Which steps each worker takes today
options_why: That is closer to a goal or a strategy. The mission is the reason to exist.
That is a detail of the plan. The mission is much wider.
That is a procedure. The mission does not list daily steps.
cards.answer: What the company is, what it does, and why it exists
cards.explanation: The mission is the place you want to reach, and why.

cards.question: A meal delivery company starts to deliver in the evening too. It hires new drivers. What changed?
options: The mission: the reason the company exists
Nothing, because the strategy never changes
The strategy: the way to reach the mission
Both, because they always change together
options_why: The company still exists to deliver meals. The reason did not change.
It is the opposite. The strategy must be flexible when the situation changes.
The mission rarely changes. The strategy is the part that adapts.
cards.answer: The strategy: the way to reach the mission
cards.explanation: The place stays the same, but the company changes the route.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”.

cards.question: A shop's mission is to sell cheap sneakers on phones. Which security plan is BEST aligned with this mission?
options: Protect the payments in a way that keeps buying quick and easy
Ask every buyer to visit the shop in person with an ID card to prove who they are
Block all phone purchases to stop fraud
Add five extra steps before every payment
options_why: This would stop most phone sales. It goes against the mission.
This is extreme. It removes the way the shop sells.
Too many steps make buying hard and lose customers. Security should help the sale.
cards.answer: Protect the payments in a way that keeps buying quick and easy
cards.explanation: Aligned security protects the business without stopping it. It helps the company sell.

cards.question: A new security manager must write the security rules. What should she do FIRST?
options: Choose the newest security tools
Copy the rules of another company
Ask each worker to write their own rules
Learn the mission and the business strategy of the company
options_why: Tools come later. The rules must first fit what the company does.
Another company has a different mission. Copied rules may not fit.
Without shared direction, every worker protects in a different way.
cards.answer: Learn the mission and the business strategy of the company
cards.explanation: You begin with a security strategy that fits the business strategy and mission.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT a sign that security is aligned with the business?
options: Security is built into the way the company works
Workers must find ways around the rules to do their jobs
Security helps the company reach its goals
The company reaches its mission thanks in part to security
options_why: This is a sign of alignment. Security is part of daily work.
This is a sign of alignment. Security is an enabler.
This is the idea of alignment in the manual.
cards.answer: Workers must find ways around the rules to do their jobs
cards.explanation: If workers must get around the rules, security is a blocker, not an enabler.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”.

cards.question: A security rule blocks the sales team. Is security a blocker or an enabler here?
cards.answer: A blocker. The rule does not fit what the company wants to do.
cards.explanation: An enabler would help the sales team to work safely.

cards.question: A company sees its security team as a brake. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The security tools are a little old
The security team has too few people to review every rule that the company writes
Workers read too few company emails
The rules were written without looking at the mission and strategy
options_why: Old tools can still help the company if the rules fit its work.
More staff does not fix rules that do not fit the business.
Emails have no direct link with security feeling like a brake.
cards.answer: The rules were written without looking at the mission and strategy
cards.explanation: Security that ignores what the company does becomes an obstacle.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”.

cards.question: Which statement about mission and strategy is true?
options: The strategy never changes, but the mission changes each year
The mission rarely changes, but the strategy must be flexible
Both must stay the same for ten years
Both change each time the market moves
options_why: It is the other way around. The strategy is the part that adapts.
The strategy must change when the business world changes.
The mission is the reason to exist. It rarely changes.
cards.answer: The mission rarely changes, but the strategy must be flexible
cards.explanation: The place you want to reach stays the same. The route changes with traffic.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”.

cards.question: What should a mission statement be used for, according to the manual?
options: To drive all company activities, including time, money, and effort
To list all the security tools that the company owns
To describe the steps of each daily task
To record the results of last year's checks
options_why: A list of tools is a detail. The mission drives everything the company does.
Steps belong to procedures. The mission is much wider.
Results belong to reports. The mission gives the direction.
cards.answer: To drive all company activities, including time, money, and effort
cards.explanation: A mission statement should drive all corporate activities.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”.

cards.question: Why should a company reach its mission thanks to security and not despite it?
cards.answer: Security should be built into the way the company works. Then it helps the company move forward.
cards.explanation: Think of an engine, not a brake.

cards.question: Which sentence describes the strategy of a company?
options: It says why the company exists
It says what the company is
It says exactly how the mission will be done
It says who owns the company and how much the owners earn
options_why: That is the mission. The strategy is about the way to do it.
That is the mission too. The strategy is the route.
Owners are not part of this idea. The strategy lists the actions to take.
cards.answer: It says exactly how the mission will be done
cards.explanation: The mission says what and why. The strategy says how.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”.

cards.question: What changes more often: the mission or the strategy?
cards.answer: The strategy. The mission rarely changes, but the strategy must change when the situation changes.
cards.explanation: You keep the place you want to reach and change the route.

cards.question: Where should a new security program start?
cards.answer: With a security strategy that fits the business strategy and the mission of the company.
cards.explanation: Security should follow the direction of the business.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”.

paragraphes: You want to pass your school year. This is your big project.
To get there, you set small steps. You study every evening. You aim for a good grade on the next test.
In a company, the big project and the small steps have two names: goal and objective.

decouverte.comme: The top of the mountain is your goal. Each stage of the walk, up to the mountain hut, is an objective.
decouverte.enVrai: A goal is something the company hopes to reach. An objective is a smaller, short-term step toward the goal. Both help the mission. The picture stops here: a company often has several goals at once.

decouverte.question: A shop wants 10,000 customers in two years. Opening a phone-friendly website in three months is...
options: A goal
An objective
A mission
decouverte.explanation: Opening the website is a short step toward the big goal of 10,000 customers. People often mix up the two words.

decouverte.texte: Goal: protect customer data all year. Objectives: train all workers about phishing before March, then update all computers every month. Phishing means fake emails that try to trick people. Each objective is a step toward the goal.

cards.question: Official definition: “goal”
cards.answer: A goal, in business, is something that an organization expects to achieve or accomplish.
cards.explanation: In simple words: a goal is the result that a company wants to reach, like the top of the mountain.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “goal”?
options: A goal, in business, is something that an organization hopes to avoid or prevent.
A goal, in business, is something that an organization expects to achieve or accomplish.
A goal, in business, is a short step that an organization expects to achieve or accomplish.
A goal, in business, is something that an individual expects to achieve or accomplish.
options_why: A goal is something to reach, not something to avoid.
A short step is an objective. A goal is the bigger result.
The sentence is about an organization, not a single person.
cards.answer: A goal, in business, is something that an organization expects to achieve or accomplish.
cards.explanation: Key words: something that an organization expects to achieve or accomplish.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “goal” from memory.
cards.answer: A goal, in business, is something that an organization expects to achieve or accomplish.
cards.explanation: Three parts: a goal, what the organization expects, and achieve or accomplish.

cards.question: Official definition: “objective”
cards.answer: An objective is a milestone or a specific step that contributes to an organization reaching its goals and achieving its mission.
cards.explanation: In simple words: an objective is one clear step on the way to a goal, like one stage of the hike.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”. A milestone is a key step, like a marker stone on a road.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “objective”?
options: An objective is a long-term result or a final target that contributes to an organization reaching its goals and achieving its mission.
An objective is a milestone or a specific step that contributes to an organization reaching its budget and achieving its profit.
An objective is a milestone or a specific plan that contributes to an organization reaching its mission and achieving its strategy.

cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Alignment of the Security Function to Business Strategy, Goals, Mission, and Objectives”.

Cancel the projects of the smallest teams
options_why: A tool can track the projects, but it cannot set the direction.
This makes the problem worse. Nobody sets one direction.
Size is not the problem. The lack of a shared direction is.
cards.answer: Form a committee of executives to set the direction
cards.explanation: A committee sets the direction of the security function.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Organizational Processes”.

cards.question: Which task is NOT a job of a governance committee?
options: Setting up the firewall rules every day
Reviewing planned security projects
Reviewing numbers that track the work
Checking that security meets stakeholder needs
options_why: This is a job of the committee. It reviews ongoing and planned projects.
This is a job of the committee. It reviews operational metrics.
This is its primary objective.
cards.answer: Setting up the firewall rules every day
cards.explanation: Daily technical work belongs to analysts, not to the committee.

cards.question: What does a governance committee do about security projects?
cards.answer: It reviews current and planned projects and gives guidance.
cards.explanation: It has an overall view, not only a technical one.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Organizational Processes”.

cards.question: Which people are MOST likely to sit on a governance committee?
options: Junior analysts who do the daily tasks
Customers who buy from the company
Executives and leaders of the company
Vendors who sell security tools
options_why: Analysts do the daily work. The committee is made of leaders.
Customers are stakeholders, but they do not lead security.
Vendors are outside the company. They do not set its direction.
cards.answer: Executives and leaders of the company
cards.explanation: A governance committee is a group of executives and leaders.

cards.question: What does a governance committee look at in its meetings?
options: Only the passwords of the users
Current and planned projects, and numbers that track the work
Only the incidents of last week
Only the invoices of the vendors
options_why: Passwords are a small detail. The committee looks at the whole picture.
Incidents matter, but the committee also looks at plans and numbers.
Invoices are not its main subject. It looks at security as a whole.
cards.answer: Current and planned projects, and numbers that track the work
cards.explanation: Committees review ongoing and planned projects, operational metrics, and other security matters.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Organizational Processes”.

cards.question: Which description fits security governance, and not the committee?
options: A group of executives that meets often
A person who does the daily security work
A tool that blocks bad traffic
All the processes that define and manage the rules, with oversight
options_why: This describes the committee, which is only a part of governance.
This describes an analyst.
This describes a firewall.
cards.answer: All the processes that define and manage the rules, with oversight
cards.explanation: Governance is the set of processes. The committee is a group of people who take part in it.

cards.question: What happens if the committee never meets?
cards.answer: Nobody checks that security follows the mission. Projects may go in many directions.
cards.explanation: The committee meets regularly to keep the course.

cards.question: Why is a committee BEST for security, compared with leaving it to tools alone?
options: Executives give direction and check that work follows the mission
Executives can replace the security team, so the tools are not needed
A committee removes the need for policies
A committee makes the tools cheaper
options_why: The team still does the work. The committee guides and checks.
Policies are still needed. The committee helps to shape them.
Cost is not the point. The point is direction and oversight.
cards.answer: Executives give direction and check that work follows the mission
cards.explanation: Tools alone are not enough. You also need oversight by executives.

cards.question: How often does a governance committee meet?
cards.answer: Regularly, not just once.
cards.explanation: The word “regularly” is in the official definition.

paragraphes: The sports club of your area and the one next door are both small. One day, the two clubs become one, with a new name.
Another time, a big club buys a small club. The small club disappears inside the big one.
In both cases, players, rules, and keys must be mixed. Companies live this too. We call it a merger or an acquisition.

decouverte.comme: Two families move into one home. Each has its own habits, keys, and wifi password. You must check everything before you mix it.
decouverte.enVrai: In a merger, two companies form one new joint company. In an acquisition, one company buys another. In both cases, you take in all the computer systems of the other company, good or bad.

decouverte.question: Your company buys a small business. What is the risk of joining the two networks right away?
options: No risk, because a small business is safe
You open the door to the security problems of the other business
You lose the mission of your company
decouverte.answer: You open the door to the security problems of the other business
decouverte.explanation: A small business is not always safe. Its systems may have weaknesses, and you inherit them.

decouverte.texte: Your company uses Windows and macOS. It buys a business with many computers that run Linux. Your team must now protect a third operating system. A new system is a new path for attackers. We call it an attack vector.
Mia was happy in her small business. After the buyout, she worries about her job. A very unhappy worker can become an insider threat. This is a person inside the company who can harm it.

Before buying, the security team reads the security rules of the other business. It checks which laws protect its data. It asks for a penetration test, or pentest. In a pentest, approved experts try to break into the systems to find weaknesses. The team also checks the open source software that the business uses. Its code is public, and its license says what you may do with it.

cards.question: Official definition: “merger”
cards.answer: A merger is the combining of two separate organizations that creates a new, joint organization.
cards.explanation: In simple words: two companies join to make one new company.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “merger”?
options: A merger is the takeover of two separate organizations that creates a new, joint organization.
A merger is the combining of two separate organizations that keeps both organizations unchanged.
A merger is the combining of two separate organizations that creates a new, joint organization.
A merger is the combining of two separate departments that creates a new, joint organization.
options_why: A takeover is the word for an acquisition. A merger is a combining.
In a merger, a new joint organization is created. Nothing stays unchanged.
A merger joins organizations, not departments.
cards.answer: A merger is the combining of two separate organizations that creates a new, joint organization.
cards.explanation: Key words: combining, two separate organizations, and a new, joint organization.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “merger” from memory.
cards.answer: A merger is the combining of two separate organizations that creates a new, joint organization.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the combining, two separate organizations, and a new, joint organization.

cards.question: Official definition: “acquisition”
cards.answer: An acquisition is the takeover of one organization by another.
cards.explanation: In simple words: one company buys another and takes control of it.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “acquisition”?
options: An acquisition is the takeover of one organization by another.
An acquisition is the combining of one organization with another.
An acquisition is the takeover of one department by another.
An acquisition is the sale of part of one organization to another.
options_why: Combining is the word for a merger. An acquisition is a takeover.
An acquisition is about organizations, not departments.
Selling a part of a company is a divestiture, not an acquisition.
cards.answer: An acquisition is the takeover of one organization by another.
cards.explanation: Key words: takeover, one organization, and by another.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “acquisition” from memory.
cards.answer: An acquisition is the takeover of one organization by another.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the takeover, one organization, and by another.

cards.question: Two companies join to form one new, joint company. What is this?
options: An acquisition
A mission statement
A merger
A security process
options_why: In an acquisition, one company takes over another. No new joint company is formed.
A mission statement says why a company exists. It is not a business event.
A security process is a repeated series of actions, not a business event.
cards.answer: A merger
cards.explanation: A merger is the combining of two separate organizations that creates a new, joint organization.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: Which risk comes from taking in the IT systems of another company?
options: The other company will have no computers
The other company will always have stronger security
Both companies will share the same weaknesses, so nothing new is added
Its systems and controls may be managed in a different way
options_why: Most companies have computers. Different systems are the real risk.
Not always. It may have weaker security or none at all.
Weaknesses may differ. The new one becomes your problem.
cards.answer: Its systems and controls may be managed in a different way
cards.explanation: You absorb the whole IT setup of the other company, good or bad.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: Why can a new operating system be a security risk after a merger?
options: It stops all the other systems
It creates a new route for attackers
It deletes the mission of the company
It makes the IT team smaller
options_why: A new system does not stop the others. It adds more to protect.
A system cannot change a mission.
The team stays the same size, but it has more to protect.
cards.answer: It creates a new route for attackers
cards.explanation: A new system is a new attack vector: one more path for attackers.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: A company wants to buy a business whose security is very different. What is the BEST step before connecting the networks?
options: Connect the networks first, to compare them faster
Replace all of their computers on the first day of the deal to be safe
Review the security of the other business and fix the key gaps first
Wait a year after the deal before looking at security
options_why: You would bring all their weaknesses into your network.
This costs a lot and is useless without first looking at what exists.
The risks must be studied before the deal, not after.
cards.answer: Review the security of the other business and fix the key gaps first
cards.explanation: If the security postures are very different, reconsider the deal or fix key gaps before connecting.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: A company plans to buy a smaller business. When should the security team join? Choose the BEST answer.
options: From the first talks until the end of the integration
After the deal is signed
After the networks are joined
Only if something goes wrong
options_why: By then, it is too late to change the deal if there are serious problems.
The weaknesses would already be inside the network.
Security should prevent problems, not wait for them.
cards.answer: From the first talks until the end of the integration
cards.explanation: The security team must be an integral part of the process from the initial talks through integration.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT an M&A risk named in the manual?
options: Unhappy employees who become an insider threat
A stretched IT team
New attack vectors
Fewer systems to protect
options_why: This is an M&A risk. Disgruntled employees can harm the company.
This is an M&A risk. The team must learn new systems and keep the old ones safe.
This is an M&A risk. New platforms mean new paths for attackers.
cards.answer: Fewer systems to protect
cards.explanation: M&A usually adds systems to protect, not fewer.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: What does “absorbing the unknown” mean in an M&A deal?
cards.answer: You take in the whole IT setup of the other company, good or bad. It may be managed differently from yours.
cards.explanation: You inherit what you did not choose.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: Mia was happy in her small company. After the buyout, she feels worried and angry. Which risk is MOST linked to this?
options: A new attack vector
An insider threat
A stretched IT team
Absorbing the unknown
options_why: A new attack vector is about new systems, not about people.
This is about the workload of IT staff, not about unhappy people.
This is about the unknown systems and controls of the other company.
cards.answer: An insider threat
cards.explanation: Corporate M&A can cause severe dissatisfaction in workers, and insider threat is a top concern.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: The IT team must learn the new systems and keep the old ones running safely. Which risk is this?
options: Creating new attack vectors: the company has new systems
Disgruntled employees
Absorbing the unknown
Impacting resources: the team is stretched thin
options_why: This is about new paths for attackers, not about the workload.
This is about people who become unhappy.
This is about unknown systems, not about how busy the team is.
cards.answer: Impacting resources: the team is stretched thin
cards.explanation: M&A is hard for everyone. IT teams may be stretched thin.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: If two security setups are very different, what should you do before connecting the networks?
cards.answer: Think again about the deal, or at least fix the key security gaps first.
cards.explanation: You do not plug a weak network into a strong one without fixing it.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: Which request shows how strong the systems of the other business are?
options: A list of the customers of the business
The results of a recent pentest, with a plan to fix serious findings
The sales results of the last year
A copy of the mission statement
options_why: A list of customers says nothing about how secure the systems are.
Sales results do not show how strong the security is.
The mission statement says why the business exists, not how secure it is.
cards.answer: The results of a recent pentest, with a plan to fix serious findings
cards.explanation: A pentest covers network, operating system, application, and database testing.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: Why check which laws apply to the data of the other business?
options: It may have to follow rules that your company does not know yet
Laws only apply to the company that buys, never to the company that sells
Laws never change after a deal
Only the lawyers need to know about it
options_why: Both companies must follow the laws that apply to their data.
A deal can bring new rules, so the new duties must be checked.
The security team needs to know too, to plan the right controls.
cards.answer: It may have to follow rules that your company does not know yet
cards.explanation: Regulations may present new requirements for your organization.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: Name two checks to do before closing an M&A deal.
cards.answer: Review the security policies of the other business, and ask for the results of a recent pentest.
cards.explanation: These checks show how mature its security is.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Mergers and Acquisitions”.

cards.question: Why is an unhappy employee a risk after a buyout?
cards.answer: They can become an insider threat: a person inside the company who can harm it.
cards.explanation: Even workers who were happy before can change.

paragraphes: You are selling your old phone. It is full of photos, messages, and passwords.
If you sell it without wiping it, the buyer can read everything.
A company that sells a part of its business has the same problem. This is called a divestiture.

decouverte.comme: Before you give your room to your brother, you take out your personal things and keep what you want.
decouverte.enVrai: A divestiture means that a company sells or gets rid of a part of its business or its assets. Assets are things that the company owns. Before the sale, you sort what leaves and what stays. Information often leaves with the computers and the buildings.

decouverte.question: A company sells its game store. What is the biggest security worry?
options: The store is sold for too high a price
Secret information leaves with the sold computers
The customers are disappointed
decouverte.answer: Secret information leaves with the sold computers
decouverte.explanation: The price and the customers matter. But for security, the biggest worry is keeping the data that leaves private.

decouverte.texte: A business sells its delivery service. Its security team lists everything that leaves: computers, software, and data. It separates these systems from the rest of the company. The manual calls this decoupling. It removes access that is no longer needed. It asks the legal team for advice.

cards.question: Official definition: “divestiture”
cards.answer: A divestiture is the act of selling off or disposing of a subset of business interests or assets.
cards.explanation: In simple words: a company sells or gets rid of a part of what it has.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “divestiture”?
options: A divestiture is the act of buying up or taking over a subset of business interests or assets.
A divestiture is the act of selling off or disposing of all business interests or assets.
A divestiture is the act of selling off or disposing of a subset of business interests or assets.
A divestiture is the act of selling off or disposing of a subset of business risks or tools.
options_why: Buying and taking over describe an acquisition. A divestiture is a sale.
It says all. A divestiture is about a subset, which means only a part.
It says risks or tools. The sentence is about business interests or assets.
cards.answer: A divestiture is the act of selling off or disposing of a subset of business interests or assets.
cards.explanation: Key words: selling off or disposing of, a subset, and business interests or assets.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “divestiture” from memory.
cards.answer: A divestiture is the act of selling off or disposing of a subset of business interests or assets.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the act of selling off or disposing, a subset, and business interests or assets.

cards.question: A company sells one of its activities. What is this called?
options: A merger
A divestiture
An acquisition
A governance committee
options_why: In a merger, two companies join. Here, the company sells a part.
In an acquisition, a company buys another. Here, the company sells.
A committee is a group of leaders. It is not a sale.
cards.answer: A divestiture
cards.explanation: A divestiture is the act of selling off or disposing of a subset of assets.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: What is the biggest security worry in a divestiture?
options: Keeping the sale price secret from the customers until the sale is signed
Making the sold computers run faster
Telling the staff about the sale
Keeping sensitive information confidential on the assets that leave
options_why: The price may matter, but the manual points to the data that leaves.
Speed is not a security worry.
Communication matters, but it is not the biggest security worry.
cards.answer: Keeping sensitive information confidential on the assets that leave
cards.explanation: Information usually goes with the assets that a company sells.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: Why might a company sell a part of its business?
options: That part no longer fits its strategy or mission
The company wants to hire more staff
The mission statement was lost
That part has too many security controls
options_why: Hiring is not a reason to sell a part of the business.
A lost document is not a reason for a sale.
Strong controls are not a reason to sell.
cards.answer: That part no longer fits its strategy or mission
cards.explanation: Divestitures often happen when a part no longer fits the strategy or mission, or after a merger creates duplicates.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: What is the first security step before a divestiture?
cards.answer: Identify and list all hardware, software, and information that are involved.
cards.explanation: You cannot protect what you do not know. First you list everything that leaves.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: A company will sell its photo service. What should the security team do FIRST?
options: Erase the data on every company computer before the sale is announced
Cut off the access of all workers
Make a list of all hardware, software, and information that leave
Send an email to all customers
options_why: Much of the data is still needed by the company.
You could block workers who still need their access. Sort first.
This is not the security priority at this stage.
cards.answer: Make a list of all hardware, software, and information that leave
cards.explanation: A complete inventory of the impacted assets is a critical first step.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: Ten workers leave with the sold service. What is the BEST action for their access?
options: Remove access that is no longer needed and keep what is still needed
Leave all access open for a few months in case the new owner has questions
Remove the access of all employees
Leave the access open until the end of the year
options_why: Access that is not needed is an open door for nothing.
The workers who stay still need their access.
Unneeded access should be removed in good time.
cards.answer: Remove access that is no longer needed and keep what is still needed
cards.explanation: This is least privilege. Remove what is not needed and leave what is needed.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: Which action is NOT one of the steps before a divestiture in the manual?
options: Identify and categorize the assets that are involved
Review all access permissions
Give the buyer full access to your shared HR and email systems
Talk to the legal and compliance teams
options_why: This is a step in the manual. It is the first one.
This is a step in the manual. You check who has access.
This is a step in the manual. They know the rules on data.
cards.answer: Give the buyer full access to your shared HR and email systems
cards.explanation: The sold assets must be separated from the shared systems, not connected to them.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: Why does information leave in a divestiture?
cards.answer: Information usually goes with the physical assets that the company sells.
cards.explanation: Think of the old phone full of photos.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: The sold systems share HR, accounting, and email with the rest of the company. What must be done?
options: Copy the shared systems to the new owner
Leave them connected to keep things simple
Switch off the shared systems for a year
Separate them from the shared systems before the sale
options_why: The new owner must not get your shared systems or data.
The new owner would keep a way into your systems.
This would stop the company from working.
cards.answer: Separate them from the shared systems before the sale
cards.explanation: The sold assets must be removed from the common systems for the new owner to run.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: In a divestiture, which company must think about its security program?
options: Only the company that sells
Both the seller and the company that gets the assets
Only the company that gets the assets, because it will own them
Neither, because the assets are gone
options_why: The other company also has to adapt its security.
The seller also has to adapt its security.
Both companies must make sure their security still works.
cards.answer: Both the seller and the company that gets the assets
cards.explanation: Each company must check that its controls and governance fit the new setup.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: Why do you separate the sold systems from the shared ones?
cards.answer: The sold assets must leave common systems, such as HR, accounting, and email, so the new owner can run them.
cards.explanation: The new owner should have no access to your systems.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: A divestiture creates a completely new company. What must the new company do?
options: Use the security team of the old company forever
Wait for the buyer to protect it
Build its own security function, with its own policies and governance
Skip policies until it makes a profit
options_why: The new company is independent. It must have its own function.
There may be no buyer. A new entity must protect itself.
Policies are needed from the start to manage information security.
cards.answer: Build its own security function, with its own policies and governance
cards.explanation: A completely new entity needs an all-new security function.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: Who is the BEST team to ask about data retention and deletion rules before a divestiture?
options: The legal and compliance teams
The sales team that talks with the buyer
The marketing team
The facilities team
options_why: Sales does not know the rules on data retention and deletion.
Marketing does not decide the legal rules for data.
Facilities manages buildings, not legal rules for data.
cards.answer: The legal and compliance teams
cards.explanation: The manual says to consult the legal and compliance teams.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

cards.question: How long should the security team take part in a divestiture?
cards.answer: From the early planning until the divestiture is complete.
cards.explanation: Early work helps the team find problems before the sale.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Divestitures”.

decouverte.titre: Who does what in a club?
paragraphes: In your sports club, the president sets the direction. The sports director leads all the teams. The coaches do the daily work.
But the rules are for every player. If one player ignores them, the whole club can have trouble.
Security works in the same way. Everyone has a role, from the chief executive to the intern.

decouverte.comme: The sports director leads all the teams. The coaches do the daily work. Every player follows the rules.
decouverte.enVrai: The CISO, the chief information security officer, leads the whole security program. A security analyst does the daily work. Every user follows the rules. A security program is the set of actions and rules that protect a company.

decouverte.question: Who is responsible for information security in a company?
options: Only the head of security
Only the IT department
Everyone, from the chief executive to the intern
decouverte.answer: Everyone, from the chief executive to the intern
decouverte.explanation: The head of security leads, but every person must follow the rules and report problems.

decouverte.titre: The roles in a small bank
decouverte.texte: Sara is the CISO. She sets the security strategy. Omar is a director. He guides several security programs. Ines runs the training program. Karim is an analyst. He sets up the firewall rules. Users also include outside workers. A contractor is hired for one job. A vendor sells products or services to the company. An intern is a student who works for a short time.

decouverte.comme: A school needs someone for the doors, the badges, and the cameras. It also needs someone to protect the files.
decouverte.enVrai: The CSO, the chief security officer, takes care of physical security and people. The CISO takes care of information. Often the CISO has both jobs. Some companies call their head of security the CSO. Always look at the context.

cards.question: Official definition: “CISO”
cards.answer: A CISO is the senior-level executive within an organization who is responsible for the overall management and supervision of the information security program.
cards.explanation: In simple words: the CISO is the top leader who runs and watches over the whole security program.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Organizational Roles and Responsibilities”. CISO means chief information security officer.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “CISO”?
options: A CISO is the senior-level executive within an organization who is responsible for the overall management and supervision of the physical security program.
A CISO is the senior-level technician within an organization who is responsible for the daily operation of the information security tools.
A CISO is a mid-level manager within an organization who is responsible for the overall management and supervision of the information security program.
A CISO is the senior-level executive within an organization who is responsible for the overall management and supervision of the information security program.
options_why: It says physical security. The CISO is about information security.
The CISO is an executive, not a technician. Daily work belongs to analysts.
The CISO is a senior-level executive, not a mid-level manager.
cards.answer: A CISO is the senior-level executive within an organization who is responsible for the overall management and supervision of the information security program.
cards.explanation: Key words: senior-level executive, overall management and supervision, and information security program.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “CISO” from memory.
cards.answer: A CISO is the senior-level executive within an organization who is responsible for the overall management and supervision of the information security program.
cards.explanation: Three parts: who they are, what they are responsible for, and over what: the information security program.

cards.question: Official definition: “CSO”
cards.answer: A CSO is a senior-level executive within an organization who is generally responsible for all physical security and personnel security matters.
cards.explanation: In simple words: the CSO takes care of the doors, the badges, and the people.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Organizational Roles and Responsibilities”. CSO means chief security officer.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “CSO”?

paragraphes: You leave your bike in front of school. If it has a lock and it is stolen, nobody blames you. If it has no lock, people say you were not careful.
People judge your actions by what a reasonable person would do in the same situation.
In a company, this idea has two names: due care and due diligence.

decouverte.comme: Putting on the lock is the first step. Checking every morning that the lock still works is the follow-up.
decouverte.enVrai: Due care means doing what a reasonable person would do to protect the assets of the company. Due diligence means checking again and again that you keep doing it. In court, you are compared with a person who has the same job and experience.

decouverte.question: A company turns on the security log of its servers. A log is a diary of what happens. Then nobody ever reads it. What is missing?
options: Due care: it did nothing
Due diligence: it does not check over time
Nothing: turning it on is enough
decouverte.answer: Due diligence: it does not check over time
decouverte.explanation: Turning on the log is due care. Reading it regularly is due diligence.

decouverte.texte: Look for weaknesses and fix them. Turn on security logs. Write strict firewall rules that follow least privilege. Least privilege means giving only the access that a job needs. A reasonable person would do these things.

Read the security logs to find anything suspicious. Run penetration tests to check that the firewall rules are strict enough. In a penetration test, approved experts try to break in. These checks are repeated again and again.
If someone sues a company, the judge asks: would a reasonable person have acted the same way? If yes, there is no negligence. Negligence means a lack of care that causes harm.
